Bacterial Speck shows dark spots on curled leaf - not matching. Let me check Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot stem with white mycelium.

The last Powdery Mildew reference shows white powdery coating on leaf surface - this white powdery appearance is the closest match to the white deposits visible on the stem in the test image.

- **Bacterial Canker**: Internal vascular browning/splitting - no match
- **Gray Mold**: Tan/brown lesions on stem - no match
- **Bacterial Speck**: Dark spots on curled leaf - no match
- **Sclerotinia**: Bleached dead stem with black sclerotia - no match
- **CMV**: Severely distorted shoestring leaves - no match
- **Powdery Mildew**: White powdery sporulation on green tissue - **closest visual match**

The white crusty/powdery deposits on the still-green stem are most consistent with Powdery Mildew, which produces white powdery sporulation that can appear on stems as well as leaves.
